newsitem.title: CHINA: Drought withers crops in northeast China province.
newsitem.headline: Drought withers crops in northeast China province.

text.p: Severe drought in China's northeastern Liaoning province has parched farmland and withered crops, but rains have eased a heatwave in eastern Shandong province, state media said on Wednesday.
Most parts of Liaoning had seen less than 10 mm of rain this summer and temperatures had averaged between two and five degrees Celsius higher than usual, the Xinhua news agency said.
The drought had affected more than 1.3 million hectares (3.2 million acres) of farmland in the province and withered 600,000 hectares (1,500,000 acres) of crops, it said.
In Shandong's Jiaodong peninsula, rain between August 2 and 4 had eased a serious drought with 30 mm in the northwestern part and 70 mm in southeastern areas, Xinhua said.

The peninsula, one of China's major grain and edible oil production bases, had been gripped by severe drought over the past two months, with Yantai city recording total precipitation of only 36 mm, a mere 10 percent of the rainfall in the same period last year, it said.
Experts had said the recent rain would help to save autumn crops but warned the dry spell was likely to continue, it said.

Unseasonably high temperatures and low rainfall across northern and northeastern China have affected a record 20 million hectares (49.4 million acres) of crops and farmland, threatening the autumn grain crop, state media has said.

Officials have said the drought was expected to cut the size of China's corn harvest this year, although overall grain production was expected to be about 484 million tonnes, only slightly below last year's record 490 million tonnes.
While drought and high temperatures have been plaguing northern China, floods have wreaked havoc in the south.
